_what: This repository's own destructive-operation policy, wired to the path the orchestrator's commands actually travel. The authority is tools/preserve.py in this tree, versioned with the capability that depends on it; nothing here modifies machine-global configuration, so no other repository, session or project is affected and this programme's correctness claims do not rest on what happens to be installed globally. The guard is a behavioural control and defence in depth -- it is not confinement, and confinement is not integrity evidence. The independent backstop stays src/hoh/integrity.py, which takes a pre/post inventory around every run.
_why: On 2026-09-23 the orchestrator ran rm -rf on a parked duplicate of a run's evidence, judging the copy redundant. Nothing unique was lost, which is luck rather than a result. The machine-global denylist allowed it and was right to by its own design rule: it blocks the catastrophic and lets recoverable local deletion through, and a duplicate under a dated run directory is indistinguishable from node_modules to a regular expression. What was missing was a definition of project- and evidence-owned that a guard could read.
_effect: A destructive command aimed at project- or evidence-owned state is refused, with the versioned-rename, archive and proven-dedupe operations named in the refusal. Ordinary cleanup (node_modules, build) stays free, replacement inside the owned scope stays free, and a command that cannot be lexed is refused only when it also names a program that destroys.
